title: The field of $\ell$-adic numbers and its valuation ring
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime number. The *$\ell$-adic valuation* $v_\ell:\mathbf Q^\times\to\mathbf Z$ sends $x=\ell^{m}\,u$, with $u$ a quotient of integers prime to $\ell$, to $m$, and the *$\ell$-adic absolute value* is $|x|_\ell=\ell^{-v_\ell(x)}$ for $x\neq0$, $|0|_\ell=0$. The field of *$\ell$-adic numbers* $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is the completion of $\mathbf Q$ with respect to $|\cdot|_\ell$; it is a complete nonarchimedean valued field of characteristic $0$, and $v_\ell$ extends to $v_\ell:\mathbf Q_\ell^\times\to\mathbf Z$ with $|x|_\ell=\ell^{-v_\ell(x)}$. The *valuation ring* of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is

$$
\mathbf Z_\ell=\{x\in\mathbf Q_\ell:|x|_\ell\leq1\}=\{0\}\cup\{x\in\mathbf Q_\ell^\times:v_\ell(x)\geq0\},
$$

the ring of *$\ell$-adic integers*; it is a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\ell\mathbf Z_\ell$ and uniformizer $\ell$, and $\mathbf Z_\ell/\ell^n\mathbf Z_\ell\cong\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ for every $n\geq1$.
